evidence: The completeness filter `completed[axis] === undefined` let `readSet: null` through at EFFORT_SCHEMA, but the reviewer's `== null` cure would refuse every default profile because `reasoningTier` defaults to a meaningful null; the agent derived nullability from `defaultEffortProfile()` and pinned both directions in a test.
guidance_note: When a check treats absence as one spelling, enumerate every spelling the same function's own comment admits (missing key and explicit null) and test each against the current schema before shipping.

evidence: The agent's grep showed `aggregateRuns` never writes `effortSchema` into scorecard-summary.json, so the fixture comment described a nonexistent producer; dropping the inert tag instead of rewording made the fixture match the real producer.
guidance_note: Before writing a fixture comment that says 'as X writes them', grep X for each field the fixture sets.

narrative: Two round-0 findings, both real. The agent correctly rejected the reviewer's `== null` cure for F1 because it would have refused the default `reasoningTier: null`, and fixed F2 by deleting the fixture's inert schema tag. Round 1 approved with no findings, so no fix produced a new finding.
guidance_observations: The agent checked the reviewer's proposed fix against the default profile before applying it and caught that it would have broken every default run.

evidence: The original `subjects = cases.map(...)` included cases with no pending job, so a complete case's foreign hit refused another case's work. The agent took the reviewer's second option (filter by names in `jobs`), which avoids a second copy of planJobs' rule.
guidance_note: When a guard's comment justifies it in terms of work about to be scheduled, derive its inputs from the plan (`jobs`), not from the selected inputs.

evidence: The original `collectMeasurements` threw on any torn run anywhere under eval/out, unlike `priorRunArms`, which only checks the root being written. The agent turned it into an `unidentified` row instead of scoping the walk or adding an escape hatch, which keeps the global scan without a global abort.
guidance_note: When an fs scan widens from one root to the whole corpus, list every way a record can fail to read (missing file, unparsable, unknown schema) and route all of them into the report vocabulary, not just the one in mind.

evidence: Same defect as F1: the `jobs.length > 0` gate scanned consultations for all cases. The reviewer's suggested `new Set(jobs.map(j => j.name))` is exactly what landed in e5a6cc7.
Same torn-record blast radius as F2. The reviewer suggested 'a non-fatal warning rather than a hard abort', and e5a6cc7 implemented that as an `unidentified` row.

The main() wiring shipped with no assertions. Reply 1 promised a test that a case with no pending job contributes no subject, but reply 2's list (ownedElsewhere, torn record, two CLI tests) leaves it out; the scoping stayed inline in main(), and F11 caught exactly that gap.
guidance_note: Before replying 'Fixed', check each test promised in the plan comment against the tests actually added, and extract any inline decision that a promised test can't reach.

evidence: The original `findRunDirsDeep` re-implemented `fs.existsSync(path.join(child, 'findings.json'))` while its comment claimed it reused `listRunDirs`. The e5a6cc7 diff injects `listRunDirs` and the restated predicate is gone.
guidance_note: When a comment claims a predicate is reused from another module, make sure that module's function is actually imported and called before writing the comment.

evidence: e5a6cc7 only guards `!fs.existsSync(metaPath)` and still calls `parseMeta(...)` unwrapped, so an unparsable meta.json or one with an unknown effortSchema still aborts every invocation. The agent's own reply concedes it 'closed the missing-file case and left the corrupt-content case wide open'.
guidance_note: When fixing an unscoped abort for one failure shape, sweep every throwing call in the same loop body (here `parseMeta`) into the same non-fatal path.

evidence: False-positive flag: the unconditional `treeIdentity(workingTree())` was already in the original f3f948e hunk, so e5a6cc7 did not introduce it. The agent applied the reviewer's primary suggestion (gate on planned work) and correctly declined the git-failure degrade, since run-case.js needs git for every replay anyway.
guidance_note: When adding a precondition-bearing step (git, corpus walk) to a command whose status path is documented as precondition-free, gate it on planned work the same way the file already gates credential resolution.

evidence: False-positive flag: `lookupMeasurement`'s min-distance tie-break is unchanged original code that e5a6cc7 did not touch. Every existing test built a single distance tier, so swapping in `Math.max` would have passed.
guidance_note: For a min/max selection, write a fixture with at least two tiers so that flipping the comparison fails a test.

evidence: False-positive flag: the unconditional corpus walk and git calls predate e5a6cc7. The original code ran them on every status re-check, which pays a full corpus walk for nothing; 14047eb moved both into `consultCorpus`, which only reads the corpus when cases are planned.
guidance_note: When adding a step whose cost grows with stored data, put it after the plan and derive it from planned work so the zero-work path stays cheap.

evidence: The F5 plan promised a test that 'a case with no pending job contributes no subject', but e5a6cc7 left `cases.filter(c => planned.has(c.name))` inline in main() and only tested `ownedElsewhere`. 14047eb extracted `plannedCases` and asserted the two-case scenario.
guidance_note: When a review fix lands, extract the exact expression that carries it into a pure function and test the reviewer's scenario against it in the same commit.

evidence: False-positive flag: the name-only `SUBJECT_FIELD` identity was in the original PR, not introduced by e5a6cc7. The agent took the reviewer's documented-constraint option and filed a record-then-key ticket, arguing correctly that keying on a fingerprint no stored run carries would make the existing 40 runs unmatchable.
guidance_note: When widening an identity's scope from one root to the whole corpus, check whether the key is still specific enough at the wider scope and state the constraint where the key is defined.

narrative: Round 0 raised six real findings in the new measurement-index wiring. In round 1, F7 is the missed remainder of the torn-record fix (unparsable meta.json), and F11 is the scoping test that the F5 plan promised and e5a6cc7 did not deliver. The other four round-1 findings were about pre-existing code, so round 1 would have happened anyway, and round 2 approved.
guidance_observations: The agent's plan comments promised more test coverage than the fix commit delivered, and the reviewer found the gap the next round.
Responses were thorough and checked each suggestion; the agent declined the reviewer's git-failure degrade with a sound reason.

evidence: `path.basename(armA.root)` is not injective, so `runsA/case-out` vs `runsB/case-out` printed identical labels and shared one default --out dir. `armLabels` keeps enough path to tell them apart, but the separator flattening applied to the --out name brought the collision back (F6).
guidance_note: When a name has two consumers (a display label and a directory name), test injectivity at each consumer, not only at the name.

evidence: `agreedInventory` compared id sets but its message printed only counts, so a same-size swap read as identical. 60908b0 prints both lists and the symmetric difference, with a test for the same-size swap.
guidance_note: Make a refusal message print the same values the check compares (sets, not their sizes).

evidence: `outcomesOf` keyed a Map by `String(id)`, so two null ids silently collapsed into one entry. The fix compares map size to `foundIds.length + missedIds.length` and refuses on mismatch, which is the reviewer's 'enforce and refuse' option.
guidance_note: When building a Map from arrays, assert map size equals input length if keys are assumed unique.

evidence: The missing misplaced-run check was real. But 60908b0 restated compare.js's rule inline under a [LAW:single-enforcer] comment, so the citation claimed one rule where the code had two copies, and F7 caught it.
guidance_note: When told to mirror a check another module already performs, extract it to a shared helper both modules import instead of copying it, and only then cite single-enforcer.

evidence: `describe()` printed only scope counts, which cannot tell two distinct same-size partitions apart. 60908b0 adds an 8-hex plan digest to the refusal and the report table, with a test.

60908b0's `slug = label.split(path.sep).join('-')` makes `ab-sweep2` and `ab/sweep2` the same directory name, reopening the default --out collision that F1 named. The fix appends a digest of the resolved roots rather than the reviewer's escaping or timestamp, which keeps the name readable, and tests the exact collision.
guidance_note: When fixing a non-injective name, check that every transformation applied after it (slugging, flattening) stays injective, and test the end-to-end output, not just the intermediate value.

evidence: The flag names 1b5404d, but the duplicate comes from the F4 fix in 60908b0, which hand-copied compare.js's `meta.case !== name` refusal into readRun. 26e68d5 extracts `requireRunCase` into score.js and both callers use it.
guidance_note: When a finding says 'mirror module X's check', make the fix import X's rule, not restate it.

evidence: False-positive flag: the bare `JSON.parse` of scorecard.json is in the original readRun hunk, and 26e68d5 did not change it. A truncated file threw a positional error with no path, and 9635b82 routes it through `parseJsonObject` with the path.
guidance_note: When one function reads several files, route every read through the same path-naming parser; grep for bare JSON.parse in that function.

evidence: 1b5404d (the F6 fix) updated the README to `paired-<armA>-vs-<armB>-<digest>` but left the USAGE `--out` default at the old name. 9635b82 aligned it.
guidance_note: When changing a default, grep for every place it is described (README, USAGE/--help, comments) and update them in the same commit.

evidence: False-positive flag: `tmpRoot` is from the original test file, not from 26e68d5. The agent measured 827 leaked `paired-test-*` dirs, and the registered `test.after` cleanup leaves zero.
guidance_note: When adding a test file, copy the sibling test files' tmp-dir cleanup convention at the same time.

evidence: False-positive flag: the `path.resolve` equality in parseArgs is original code. Symlinked roots got past it and paired an arm with itself, reporting p=1. The agent moved the check to `pairArms` over `fs.realpathSync` roots so parseArgs stays pure, and tested it with a real symlink.
guidance_note: When a guard compares paths for identity, compare canonical (realpath) values at the point where the filesystem is already being read.

evidence: `agreedArmEffort` predates the review, but it is the same duplicated-rule class the F7 fix consolidated one function over without sweeping; the agent concedes 'I extracted that rule and then left this one hand-rolled beside it'. The extraction also exposed that the pre-rendered effort string made the check compare a value against itself, which a test caught.
guidance_note: When consolidating one duplicated rule into a shared helper, grep the same files for every other rule whose comment says 'same rule as X' and consolidate them in the same commit.

narrative: Round 0 raised five real findings in the new paired reducer. Round 1's only finding (F6) re-opened F1's collision through the slug step, and round 2's only finding (F7) was the duplicate rule the F4 fix hand-copied, so both rounds were avoidable. Round 3 combined fix fallout (F9 USAGE drift from F6, F12 the unswept sibling of F7) with pre-existing issues, round 4 posted only an out-of-diff Bearer-auth claim that the agent disproved, and round 5 hit the review-round cap.
guidance_observations: Two of three fix chains came from fixes that copied or re-derived a rule instead of sharing it, and each copy was found the next round.
The round cap was reached partly because rounds 1 and 2 each existed only to catch a defect in the previous fix.
